Linear parabolic problems

Source: R/heat.R
parabolic_problem.Rd

parabolic_problem() defines

Usage

parabolic_problem(
  mesh,
  diffusion = 1,
  reaction = 0,
  advection = NULL,
  source = 0,
  initial = 0,
  bcs = list(),
  time = c(0, 1),
  degree = 1,
  stabilization = c("none", "supg"),
  quad_degree = NULL
)

heat_problem(
  mesh,
  diffusivity = 1,
  source = 0,
  initial = 0,
  bcs = list(),
  time = c(0, 1),
  degree = 1
)

Arguments

mesh

A pde_mesh().

diffusion

Diffusion coefficient k.

reaction

Reaction coefficient c (non-negative for coercivity).

advection

Velocity b, or NULL.

source

Source f.

initial

Initial condition: number, function(x, y) or fe_function().

bcs

A pde_bc or list of them. Boundary edges without a condition receive the natural condition k du/dn = 0.

time

Start and end time.

degree

Lagrange degree (1 or 2).

stabilization

"none" or "supg".

quad_degree

Quadrature exactness degree (default 2 degree + 2).

diffusivity

Diffusivity kappa of the heat equation.

Value

An object of class parabolic_problem.

Details

du/dt - div(k grad u) + b . grad u + c u = f(x, y, t) for t in (time[1], time[2]), with u(x, y, time[1]) = initial(x, y) and boundary conditions whose data may depend on time (function(x, y, t)). Scalar diffusion, advection and reaction coefficients may also depend on time (function(x, y, t)); the operator is then reassembled and refactorized at every step, with A(t_{n+1}) on the implicit side and A(t_n) on the explicit side of the theta scheme (second order for Crank-Nicolson). Otherwise the matrices are assembled and factorized once. The Rannacher startup steps are skipped for time-dependent coefficients. SUPG requires time-independent coefficients.

heat_problem() is the heat equation du/dt - kappa Laplace(u) = f.

The finite-element semidiscretization is M du/dt + A u = F(t) with mass matrix M and operator matrix A (including Robin terms). Time stepping uses the theta method; see solve_pde() arguments dt and method.

Examples

mesh <- pde_mesh_rectangle(nx = 8)
prob <- heat_problem(mesh, diffusivity = 1,
                     initial = function(x, y) sin(pi * x) * sin(pi * y),
                     bcs = dirichlet_bc(0), time = c(0, 0.1))
sol <- solve_pde(prob, dt = 0.01)
sol
#> <pde_transient> P1, 81 dofs, 10 steps of crank-nicolson (dt =  0.01)
#>   stored times: 11 in [    0,   0.1]
